source.title: Representational Alignment Across Model Layers and Brain Regions with Hierarchical Optimal Transport

record.tranche_reason: Tests representational alignment and cross-model mapping with a different measure and method: hierarchical optimal transport and held-out reconstruction correlation, including a rotation-augmented variant.
record.gate_note: The study measures alignment and reconstruction across model pairs, but does not test whether alignment rises with model scale and capability. It does not use paired image-caption data. The Pythia checkpoint-trajectory result is figure-only and concerns checkpoint correspondences, not shared features or subspaces; it is not extracted as a row. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper proposing Multi-Level OT (MOT). It still reports held-out reconstruction correlations between independently trained models: LLM pairs (Table 1, Table H.1) and ViT pairs (Tables 3, D.1, D.2). These numbers bear on V4, whether one model maps onto another with little loss. Scores for the same pairs vary sharply with the alignment method: rotation-sensitive vs rotation-augmented OT, and OT vs linear predictivity. That bears on V6. No alignment-vs-scale trend, image-caption pairing or feature universality is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. In vision, vanilla MOT does not consistently beat pairwise OT; only MOT+R clearly surpasses the baselines. In cortex-cortex comparisons MOT only matches pairwise OT. The authors present MOT as a measurement tool and explicitly do not address why systems converge.
record.recipe_differences: Uses hierarchical optimal transport and held-out activation reconstruction rather than the original sources' similarity analyses; adds soft layer-to-layer transport and an optional rotation-augmented variant.
record.method_sensitivity: For vision-model comparisons, rotation augmentation substantially changes reconstruction scores and improves them. The authors also report that vanilla MOT's layer correspondences are only partial in some cases, while MOT + R yields clearer correspondences. LLM and fMRI analyses omit rotation augmentation because of computational cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Human visual cortex (NSD fMRI, 4 subjects) maps onto DINOv2/ViT-MAE layers with low held-out reconstruction correlation: 0.07–0.13 with MOT, 0.15–0.16 with MOT+R. Transport plans show partial, inconsistent hierarchy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Brain-model representational alignment, measured by unit-level transport reconstruction, is weak but improves with rotation invariance.

fits_no_version.finding: MOT transport plans recover near-diagonal layer hierarchies across models of different depth. Hierarchy scores are 0.83–0.96 for LLMs and 0.83–0.95 for MOT+R on ViTs (Table G.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-wise ordering of representations is preserved across independently trained models.

record.problems: The study evaluates a limited set of models and datasets, and explicitly notes computational constraints for rotation optimization on LLM and fMRI data. It measures reconstruction correlation rather than model capability or the proposed scale-performance trend; the text does not establish why the observed alignments arise.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit is reached. Omitted LLM Random (Perm-P) and Single-Best OT table results; vision-cortex per-subject values in Tables E.2 and E.3; cortex-to-cortex comparisons; and figure-only transport-plan details, including Pythia checkpoint trajectory alignment (Figure 5). The Pythia result is described in text as a coherent checkpoint correspondence, but it does not measure shared features or subspaces.

untested.parts: No alignment-vs-scale or alignment-vs-capability trend is analysed. Model sizes vary, but only individual pair scores are reported.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
The Pythia-14M seed1 vs seed2 analysis (Fig. 5) shows only figure-level checkpoint correspondence. It does not test shared features or subspaces.
Untested: stitching, relative representations and mapping without paired data. Rotation-augmented mappings were not run for LLMs.
No interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
Untested: neighbour count and out-of-distribution inputs. Only one dataset is used per domain.
Plateau and the role of shared data or objectives are not tested. The authors explicitly put 'why systems converge' out of scope.

missing.what: Pairwise linear-predictivity reconstruction scores for the six LLM pairs (0.694–0.848) vs MOT (0.383–0.558). This is the largest metric-dependence contrast in the paper.
Neuron sub-sampling: MOT+R keeps about 0.5 reconstruction with 10% of Llama neurons; scores rise with fraction kept.
Hierarchy scores for the MOT, pairwise and rotation transport plans.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a methods paper, and many rows (the -P/-PR baselines) exist to compare the authors' method with others. They still record model-model mapping quality, so they are kept for V4. The study's evidence on convergence is incidental. Its strongest bearing is on V6: the same pair's alignment score and rank depend heavily on rotation invariance and on OT vs linear predictivity. LLM rotation-augmented results were not run because of compute cost.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether alignment increases as independently trained models become larger or more capable; model sizes are compared, but no alignment-versus-scale/performance trend is evaluated.
No vision-language model comparison using paired images and captions.
The Pythia seed-1/seed-2 analysis reports checkpoint-level trajectory correspondences, not whether the networks learn the same features or shared subspaces.
Tests OT-based mappings with shared stimuli and held-out reconstruction; does not test mapping without paired data, stitching, or relative representations.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.

Tests differences associated with rotation-sensitive versus rotation-augmented alignment in the reported vision comparisons; does not systematically vary neighbour count, other metric settings, or in-/out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it.
